p.src: Now, when Xue Pan heard this, his anger gradually subsided. Three or five days later, though the pain had gone, the marks of his injuries remained; so he stayed at home pretending to be ill, too ashamed to face his relatives and friends.

p.src: In the blink of an eye it was already the tenth month. Some clerks from the various shops had completed the yearly accounts and were due to return home, so the household naturally prepared a farewell feast for them. Among them was a man named Zhang Dehui, now over sixty, who had managed the Xue family pawnshops since his youth. He had property worth two or three thousand taels of silver to live on at home, and this year he too was going home, not to return until the following spring. In the course of conversation he said, “Paper goods and incense materials have been scarce this year, so they are certain to be expensive next year. Next year I shall first send my elder and younger sons up here to look after the pawnshop, while I buy paper goods and scented fans along my route and bring them here to sell before the Dragon Boat Festival. Even after customs duties and expenses are deducted, I should still make several times my investment in profit.” Hearing this, Xue Pan thought to himself, “Now that I have been beaten, I can hardly show my face. I have been wanting to hide away for a year or so, but have nowhere to go. Pretending to be ill every day is no solution either. Besides, I have grown this old without becoming either a scholar or a warrior. Though I claim to be in business, I have never so much as handled a steelyard or an abacus, and I know nothing of local customs or of which roads are near or far. I might as well put together some capital and travel about with Zhang Dehui for a year. Whether I make money or not, at least I can escape my embarrassment for a while. And besides, it would be pleasant to see some mountains and rivers.” His mind made up, he told Zhang Dehui after the feast had ended and asked him to wait a day or two so that they could set out together.

p.src: That evening Xue Pan told his mother. Aunt Xue was pleased to hear it, yet feared that he might cause trouble while away; losing the capital would have been a minor matter by comparison. She therefore refused to let him go. “Whatever happens,” she said, “if you remain here with me, I shall at least feel more at ease. Besides, there is no need for you to undertake this trade; we are not waiting upon those few hundred taels for our livelihood. If you behave yourself and keep out of trouble at home, that is worth more than those few hundred taels.” But Xue Pan had made up his mind and would not listen. He said, “Every day you tell me that I know nothing of the world, understand nothing, and refuse to learn anything. Now I have firmly resolved to give up all those worthless pursuits and intend to make a man of myself by learning to conduct business, yet you refuse to allow that too. What do you expect me to do? I am not a maidservant to be shut up at home. When would such a life ever end? Besides, Zhang Dehui is an elderly and virtuous man, and our families have been friends for generations. If I go with him, how could anything go amiss? Even if I should stray briefly into some improper place, he would naturally warn and remonstrate with me. He knows the prices and market conditions of every sort of merchandise, so I could consult him about everything. Nothing could be more convenient, yet still you will not let me go. In a couple of days I shall make my preparations and leave without telling anyone at home. When I return rich next year, then you will see what I am capable of.” Having said this, he went off to bed in a huff.

p.src: After hearing him speak this way, Aunt Xue discussed the matter with Baochai. Baochai smiled and said, “If Brother truly wishes to gain experience in serious affairs, that is certainly a good thing. The only trouble is that, though he speaks well while at home, once he is away his old habits may return, and then he will be even harder to restrain. But there is no use worrying so much. If he truly reforms, it will be a blessing for the rest of his life. If he does not, Mother has no other means of changing him. We can only do what lies within human power and leave the rest to Heaven. He is a grown man. If we continually fear that he knows nothing of the ways of the world and therefore cannot leave home or undertake any business, then after being shut up this year he will remain exactly the same next year. Since his reasons are perfectly respectable, Mother should simply reckon upon losing eight hundred or a thousand taels and hand it over to let him try his hand. In any case, the clerks will be there to help him, and surely they would be too ashamed to deceive him outright. Moreover, once he is away, he will have no companions to encourage his pleasures and no one on whom to rely. Out in the world, no one will stand in awe of anyone else: when he has money he will eat, and when he has none he will go hungry, with no one to turn to wherever he looks. When he sees what life is like, he may perhaps cause less trouble than he does at home.” After pondering Baochai's words for a long while, Aunt Xue said, “What you say is right. It would be worth spending some money if it taught him to behave sensibly.” The matter settled, nothing further occurred that night. The next day Aunt Xue sent for Zhang Dehui. She had Xue Pan entertain him with food and wine in the study, while she herself stood in the rear corridor and, speaking through the window, repeatedly and earnestly entrusted Xue Pan to Zhang Dehui's care. Zhang Dehui readily promised everything. After eating, he took his leave, then turned back to say, “The fourteenth is a most auspicious day for travel. Young Master should prepare his luggage and hire the mules at once, and we shall set off early on the morning of the fourteenth.” Xue Pan was overjoyed and reported these words to Aunt Xue. Aunt Xue, Baochai, Xiangling, and two elderly nurses spent the next several days preparing his traveling gear. They assigned him an old servant who had been his foster father, two long-serving retainers experienced in worldly affairs, and two pages who habitually attended him in person—six masters and servants altogether. They hired three large carts solely for the luggage and equipment, as well as four mules for the long journey. Xue Pan himself would ride a large, swift, iron-gray mule raised in the household, with a saddle horse held in reserve. Once all the preparations were complete, Aunt Xue, Baochai, and the others admonished him far into the night; there is no need to repeat all their advice. On the thirteenth, Xue Pan first went to take leave of his maternal uncle and then came over to bid farewell to everyone in the Jia household. Jia Zhen and the others naturally spoke of holding another farewell feast, but that need not be described in detail. Early on the morning of the fourteenth, Aunt Xue, Baochai, and the others accompanied Xue Pan all the way out through the ceremonial gate. Mother and daughter watched him depart with four tearful eyes before turning back.

p.src: When Aunt Xue came to the capital, she had brought only four or five families of servants, along with two or three elderly maids and young girls. Now that most of them had gone with Xue Pan, only one or two men remained outside. That same day, therefore, Aunt Xue went to the study and had all its furnishings, ornaments, curtains, and other articles moved inside and stored away. She also ordered the wives of the two men who had accompanied Xue Pan to move inside to sleep. She further told Xiangling to secure her own room carefully. “Lock the door and come sleep with me tonight.” Baochai said, “Since you already have all these people to keep you company, Mother, why not let Sister Ling come and stay with me? It is quiet in our garden, and the nights are growing long. I work every evening, so surely the more company I have, the better.” Aunt Xue laughed when she heard this. “Of course! I had forgotten. She ought to go with you. Only the other day I told your brother that Wenxing is still young and talks without rhyme or reason, while Ying'er cannot manage all the attendance alone, so we ought to buy another maid for you.” Baochai replied, “With someone bought from strangers, we would know nothing of her background. If we chose badly, wasting the money would be a small matter; the real trouble would be all the vexation she caused. It would be better to inquire at leisure and buy one only when we find someone whose origins are known.” As she spoke, she had Xiangling pack her bedding and toilet case, then ordered an old maid and Zhen'er to take them to Allspice Court. Only then did Baochai and Xiangling return to the garden together.

p.src: Xiangling said, “I had meant to ask Madam myself whether, now that Master has gone away, I might come and keep you company. But I was afraid she might take it amiss and think I merely wanted to come amuse myself in the garden. Who would have thought you would propose it yourself?” Baochai laughed. “I know you have longed to live in this garden for more than a day or two; you simply never had the opportunity. Even when you came once a day, you were always rushing about, so there was little pleasure in it. So take this opportunity and simply stay for a whole year. I shall gain a companion, and you will have your wish.” Xiangling smiled. “Dear Miss, while you have the chance, do teach me how to write poetry.” Baochai laughed. “I knew that, after gaining Long, you would set your sights on Shu! Since this is your first day here, I advise you to go out through the garden's east corner gate and pay your respects everywhere, beginning with the Old Lady. There is no need to make a point of telling them that you have moved into the garden. If anyone happens to ask why, merely mention in passing that I brought you here to keep me company, and leave it at that. When you return to the garden, go and call on each of the young ladies as well.”

p.src: Xiangling assented and was just about to leave when Ping'er came hurrying in. Xiangling hastened to greet her, and Ping'er could only return the greeting with a smile. Baochai smiled at Ping'er and said, “I have brought her here today to keep me company and was just going to send word to your mistress.” Ping'er laughed. “What a thing to say, Miss! You leave me quite at a loss for an answer.” Baochai said, “But that is only proper. An inn has its proprietor and a temple its abbot. Though this is no great matter, word should still be given. Then the night watchmen in the garden will know that two more people have been added and can properly shut the gates and keep watch over the doors. Tell her when you go back; then I need not send anyone specially.” Ping'er agreed, then smiled at Xiangling. “Now that you have moved in, are you not going to pay your respects to all your neighbors?” Baochai laughed. “That is precisely where I am sending her.” Ping'er said, “You need not come to our place just yet. Second Master is ill at home.” Xiangling assented and went off, beginning with Grandmother Jia. There is no need to dwell on this.

p.src: Now, after Xiangling had left, Ping'er caught hold of Baochai and said urgently, “Miss, have you heard our latest news?” Baochai replied, “I have heard no news. For the past few days I have been busy seeing my brother off, so I know nothing at all of what has happened here. I have not even seen the other girls these last two days.” Ping'er said with a rueful smile, “Master beat Second Master so badly that he cannot move. Can it be that you have not heard?” Baochai said, “I vaguely heard some mention of it early this morning, but I could not believe it. I was just intending to visit your mistress when you arrived. What was he beaten for this time?” Clenching her teeth, Ping'er cursed, “It is all because of that Jia Yucun—or whatever ‘Fengcun’ he calls himself—that half-starved mongrel who came from nowhere! They have known him for less than ten years, yet how much trouble he has caused! This spring, Master happened to see several antique fans somewhere. When he came home, none of the fine fans in his own collection seemed worth anything to him, and he immediately ordered people to search everywhere for more. As fate would have it, there was an obstinate fellow popularly nicknamed Stone Simpleton. He was so poor that he had nothing to eat, yet he owned twenty antique fans and absolutely refused to let them leave his house. After calling in countless favors, Second Master finally managed to meet the man. After much persuasion, the fellow invited Second Master into his house and brought out the fans for him to inspect briefly. According to Second Master, there could be no finer examples: their frames were all made of mottled bamboo, coir bamboo, deer-horn bamboo, or jade bamboo, and every painting and inscription was an authentic work by an ancient master. So he came back and told Master. Master then told him to buy them and to pay whatever price the man asked. But that Stone Simpleton declared, ‘I would sooner starve or freeze to death! I would not sell them even for a thousand taels apiece!’ Master could do nothing and cursed Second Master every day for being useless. Second Master had already offered him five hundred taels, with payment in silver before delivery of the fans. But he simply would not sell, insisting, ‘If you want my fans, you must take my life first!’ Just think, Miss—what could anyone do about that? Then that godless Yucun heard of the matter and devised a scheme. He falsely accused the man of owing money to the government and hauled him before the magistrate. On the pretext that his property must be sold to repay the arrears, the fans were confiscated, assessed at an official price, and delivered here. No one knows whether Stone Simpleton is alive or dead now. Holding the fans, Master asked Second Master, ‘How did he manage to obtain them?’ Second Master merely replied, ‘Driving a man to ruin and destroying his family over such a trifling matter is hardly anything to boast of!’ Master flew into a rage on hearing this, saying that Second Master had deliberately spoken to rebuke him. That was the first serious charge against him.

p.src: There were several other minor incidents these past few days, but I cannot remember them clearly; they were all lumped together, and then the beating began. They did not drag her down and use a board or cudgel; they simply made her stand there and gave her a wild beating with I know not what, cutting her face in two places. We heard that Her Ladyship has a kind of pill here for treating wounds from beatings. Miss, please find one for me at once.” On hearing this, Baochai promptly told Ying'er to ask for a pill and give it to Ping'er. Baochai said, “Since that is what happened, give her my regards. I shall not go myself.” Ping'er assented and left; there is no more to be said of this.

p.src: Now, after Xiangling had greeted everyone and eaten supper, Baochai and the others went to Grandmother Jia's quarters, while she herself made her way to the Naiad's House. By then Daiyu had largely recovered, and she was naturally delighted to see that Xiangling too had come to live in the Garden. Xiangling said with a smile, “Now that I have moved in here, I have some leisure at last. If you would only teach me to write poetry, it would be the greatest good fortune of my life!” Daiyu laughed. “If you want to write poetry, then take me as your teacher. Though I know little myself, I can still teach you the rudiments.” Xiangling laughed. “If you truly mean it, I shall take you as my teacher. But you must promise not to grow tired of me.” Daiyu said, “What is so difficult about it that it even needs studying? It is merely a matter of introduction, development, transition, and conclusion. The development and transition in the middle comprise two antithetical couplets: level tones match oblique ones, function words match substantive words, and substantive words match function words. But if you produce a truly remarkable line, it does not matter even if its tones and word classes fail to correspond.” Xiangling smiled. “No wonder! I often take up an old anthology and read a poem or two whenever I have a spare moment. Some have perfectly wrought antitheses, while others do not; and I have also heard it said, ‘Pay no heed to the first, third, and fifth; distinguish clearly the second, fourth, and sixth.’ Yet in the poems of the ancients I find some that follow the rule and others that violate it in the second, fourth, or sixth position, so I have been puzzled day after day. Now that I have heard your explanation, I see that these patterns and rules are secondary after all, and that freshness and originality of expression matter most.” Daiyu said, “That is precisely the principle. Yet words and phrases are secondary too; what matters above all is the conception. If the feeling and idea are genuine, the poem will naturally be fine even without embellishing its language. This is what is meant by ‘not allowing words to harm the meaning.’” Xiangling smiled. “I especially love Lu Fangweng's lines, ‘The layered blinds stay unraised, preserving the fragrance long; the ancient inkstone's shallow hollow gathers ample ink.’ They are truly delightful!” Daiyu said, “You must on no account imitate poetry of that kind. Because you know nothing of poetry, you are pleased by such facile lines; once you fall into that mold, you will never progress beyond it. Just listen to me. If you sincerely wish to learn, I have here the Complete Works of Wang Mojie. First read a hundred of his regulated five-character poems and ponder them carefully until you know them thoroughly. Then read one or two hundred of Old Du's regulated seven-character poems, followed by one or two hundred of Li Qinglian's seven-character quatrains. Once these three poets have furnished a foundation within you, you may go on to read Tao Yuanming, Ying Yang, Xie, Ruan, Yu, Bao, and the others. You are exceptionally quick and intelligent; in less than a year, you are sure to become an accomplished poet!” After hearing this, Xiangling smiled and said, “In that case, dear miss, please bring out the book and lend it to me. I can take it back and read a few poems tonight.”

u.src: Now, after Xiangling had greeted everyone and eaten supper, Baochai and the others went to Grandmother Jia's quarters, while she herself made her way to the Naiad's House.
By then Daiyu had largely recovered, and she was naturally delighted to see that Xiangling too had come to live in the Garden.
Xiangling said with a smile, “Now that I have moved in here, I have some leisure at last. If you would only teach me to write poetry, it would be the greatest good fortune of my life!”
Daiyu laughed. “If you want to write poetry, then take me as your teacher.
Though I know little myself, I can still teach you the rudiments.”
Xiangling laughed. “If you truly mean it, I shall take you as my teacher.
But you must promise not to grow tired of me.”
Daiyu said, “What is so difficult about it that it even needs studying?

It is merely a matter of introduction, development, transition, and conclusion. The development and transition in the middle comprise two antithetical couplets: level tones match oblique ones, function words match substantive words, and substantive words match function words. But if you produce a truly remarkable line, it does not matter even if its tones and word classes fail to correspond.”

Xiangling smiled. “No wonder! I often take up an old anthology and read a poem or two whenever I have a spare moment. Some have perfectly wrought antitheses, while others do not; and I have also heard it said, ‘Pay no heed to the first, third, and fifth; distinguish clearly the second, fourth, and sixth.’
Yet in the poems of the ancients I find some that follow the rule and others that violate it in the second, fourth, or sixth position, so I have been puzzled day after day.
Now that I have heard your explanation, I see that these patterns and rules are secondary after all, and that freshness and originality of expression matter most.”
Daiyu said, “That is precisely the principle. Yet words and phrases are secondary too; what matters above all is the conception.
If the feeling and idea are genuine, the poem will naturally be fine even without embellishing its language. This is what is meant by ‘not allowing words to harm the meaning.’”

Xiangling smiled. “I especially love Lu Fangweng's lines, ‘The layered blinds stay unraised, preserving the fragrance long; the ancient inkstone's shallow hollow gathers ample ink.’ They are truly delightful!”
Daiyu said, “You must on no account imitate poetry of that kind.
Because you know nothing of poetry, you are pleased by such facile lines; once you fall into that mold, you will never progress beyond it.

u.src: Just listen to me. If you sincerely wish to learn, I have here the Complete Works of Wang Mojie. First read a hundred of his regulated five-character poems and ponder them carefully until you know them thoroughly. Then read one or two hundred of Old Du's regulated seven-character poems, followed by one or two hundred of Li Qinglian's seven-character quatrains.
Once these three poets have furnished a foundation within you, you may go on to read Tao Yuanming, Ying Yang, Xie, Ruan, Yu, Bao, and the others.
You are exceptionally quick and intelligent; in less than a year, you are sure to become an accomplished poet!”
After hearing this, Xiangling smiled and said, “In that case, dear miss, please bring out the book and lend it to me. I can take it back and read a few poems tonight.”

p.src: At this, Daiyu told Zijuan to bring Wang Youcheng's regulated five-character poems and handed them to Xiangling, saying, “All those marked with a red circle are ones I selected. Read them one by one. If there is anything you do not understand, ask your mistress; or if you happen to meet me, I shall explain it to you.” Taking the book of poems, Xiangling returned to Allspice Court. Neglecting everything else, she sat beneath the lamp and began reading the poems one after another. Baochai repeatedly urged her to go to bed, but she would not sleep. Seeing how earnestly she applied herself, Baochai had no choice but to let her be.

p.src: One day, just as Daiyu had finished washing and dressing, Xiangling appeared with a beaming smile to return the book and ask to exchange it for Du's regulated poems. Daiyu asked with a smile, “How many poems have you memorized altogether?” Xiangling replied with a smile, “I have read every poem marked with a red circle.” Daiyu asked, “Have you grasped any of their flavor?” Xiangling smiled. “I have grasped a little, though I do not know whether I am right. Let me tell you what I think.” Daiyu smiled. “Only by studying and discussing poetry can one improve. Go on, then; let me hear.” Xiangling smiled. “As I see it, the beauty of poetry lies in meanings that cannot be expressed in words, yet become vividly true when one reflects upon them. Some lines seem unreasonable, yet on reflection prove both reasonable and full of feeling.” Daiyu smiled. “There is something in what you say, but where did you perceive it?” Xiangling smiled. “I was reading his poem ‘On the Frontier,’ which contains the couplet: ‘Over the vast desert, a solitary plume of smoke rises straight; above the long river, the setting sun hangs round.’ When one thinks about it, how can smoke be straight? And the sun is round by nature: the word ‘straight’ seems unreasonable, while ‘round’ seems far too commonplace. Yet when I close the book and reflect, it is as though I have seen the scene with my own eyes. If one tried to find two other words to replace them, no alternatives could be found at all. Then there are the lines, ‘At sunset, river and lake turn white; as the tide comes in, heaven and earth grow blue.’ The words ‘white’ and ‘blue’ likewise seem unreasonable. Yet on reflection, only those two words can fully convey the scene; when spoken aloud, each seems like an olive weighing several thousand catties. There are also the lines, ‘At the ferry remains the setting sun; from the village rises solitary smoke.’ How ever did he think of the words ‘remains’ and ‘rises’! The year we came to the capital, our boat moored toward evening one day. There was no one on the bank, only a few trees; far away, smoke rose from several households cooking supper. That smoke was actually blue-green and climbed straight up until it met the clouds. Who would have thought that when I read those two lines last night, I felt as though I had returned to that very place?”

p.src: As they were speaking, Baoyu and Tanchun arrived and also sat down to hear her discourse on poetry. Baoyu laughed. “If you understand that, there is no need to read any more poems. True understanding does not depend on quantity. From those two remarks of yours, it is clear that you have already grasped the secret.” Daiyu laughed. “You praise his phrase ‘rises the lonely smoke,’ but you do not know that even this line was modeled on an earlier poet. Let me show you another line, one even more understated and natural than this.” With that, she found Tao Yuanming’s lines, “Dim in the distance lies a village of men; faintly, smoke drifts above the hamlet,” and handed them to Xiangling. Xiangling read them, nodded in admiration, and said with a smile, “So the word ‘rises’ was transformed from the two words ‘drifts faintly.’” Baoyu burst out laughing. “You have understood it already. There is no need for any more explanation, or your learning will only become muddled. Just begin composing; your poem is sure to be good.” Tanchun laughed. “Tomorrow I shall send you a formal invitation to join our poetry club.” Xiangling laughed. “Why tease me, miss? I only admired what you did and wanted to try it for amusement.” Tanchun and Daiyu both laughed. “Who among us is doing anything but amusing herself? Do you suppose we compose poetry in earnest? If we claimed that our earnest efforts had produced real poetry, people outside this garden would laugh their teeth out.” Baoyu said, “That is sheer self-contempt and defeatism. The other day, when I was outside discussing the paintings with some gentlemen, they heard that we had founded a poetry club and begged me to show them our manuscripts. I copied out several poems for them, and every one of them was sincerely filled with admiration. They all copied them out and took them away to have them printed.” Tanchun and Daiyu hurriedly asked, “Is that really true?” Baoyu laughed. “If anyone is lying, it is the parrot on that perch.” On hearing this, Daiyu and Tanchun both cried, “You really are outrageous! Never mind that those verses are hardly poetry—even if they were, writings from our brushes ought not to be circulated outside.” Baoyu said, “What is there to fear? Because the writings of women’s chambers were never allowed to circulate in ancient times, no one knows of them today.” As he spoke, Xichun sent Ruhua to summon him, and only then did Baoyu leave. Xiangling then pressed Daiyu to bring out Du Fu’s regulated verse and implored both Daiyu and Tanchun, “Give me a subject so that I may cobble together a poem. When I bring it back, please correct it for me.” Daiyu said, “Last night’s moon was at its loveliest. I meant to cobble together a poem about it but could not finish one, so you compose one instead. Use the rhyme category ‘Fourteen Han,’ choosing whichever words from it you please.”

p.src: After hearing this, Xiangling returned in silence. This time she would not even enter her room, but remained beneath the trees beside the pond, now sitting on a rock lost in thought, now crouching on the ground and scratching at the earth, to the amazement of all who passed. When Li Wan, Baochai, Tanchun, Baoyu, and the others heard of this, they stood at a distance on the hillside and watched her. They saw her knit her brows one moment, then smile to herself the next. Baochai laughed. “She is surely going mad! Last night she muttered and fretted until the fifth watch before finally falling asleep, and day broke in less time than it takes to eat a meal. Then I heard her get up, hastily do her hair, and hurry off to find Pin’er. After she came back, she spent the whole day in a daze. She composed one poem and it was no good, so naturally she is now composing another.” Baoyu laughed. “This is precisely what is meant by ‘a numinous land produces exceptional people.’ Heaven never endows anyone with sensibility and passion in vain. Every day we lamented that it was a pity for such a person as her to remain commonplace, yet who could have known that this day would come at last? This shows that Heaven and Earth are perfectly just.” Baochai laughed. “If only you could apply yourself as painstakingly as she does, what could you possibly fail to learn?” Baoyu made no reply.

p.src: Baochai laughed. “It does not sound like a poem about the moon. If you added the word ‘light’ after ‘moon,’ it might pass, for every line is really about moonlight. Still, it will do. Poetry begins with talking nonsense; give yourself a few more days and you will improve.” Xiangling had thought her poem supremely fine. Disheartened by these remarks but unwilling to let the matter drop, she began pondering again. Seeing the young ladies chatting and laughing, she went out alone to pace beneath the bamboo before the steps, racking her brains, hearing nothing around her and looking at nothing else. Presently Tanchun called through the window with a laugh, “Miss Ling, do take it easy for a while.” Xiangling answered absently, “‘Xian’ belongs to the fifteenth rhyme group, Shan. You have used the wrong rhyme.” At this, everyone burst out laughing. Baochai said, “She truly is possessed by the poetry demon. That may bring her to her senses.”

p.src: After they had all gone their separate ways, Xiangling’s mind remained wholly occupied with poetry. That evening she sat staring blankly at the lamp for a long while. She did not lie down until after the third watch, and then remained wide awake until she finally drifted into a hazy sleep at the fifth watch. When day broke, Baochai awoke and listened. Hearing Xiangling sleeping soundly, she thought, “She tossed and turned all night. I wonder whether she managed to finish it. She must be exhausted now, so I had better not wake her.” As she was thinking this, she suddenly heard Xiangling laugh in her sleep. “I have it at last! Surely this poem cannot still be bad?” Baochai found this both pitiable and amusing. She quickly woke Xiangling and asked, “What have you found? Such devotion has almost given you communion with the immortals. If you fail to learn poetry, you will have made yourself ill besides.” As she spoke, she washed and dressed, then joined the other young ladies and went to Grandmother Jia’s apartments. Xiangling had applied herself so painfully to the study of poetry, concentrating all her vitality and sincerity upon it, that although she could compose nothing by day, eight lines suddenly came to her in a dream. As soon as she had washed and dressed, she hurriedly wrote the lines down. Unable to judge whether they were good or bad, she took them and went to seek Daiyu again. She had just reached the Fragrant Stream Pavilion when she saw Li Wan and the other young ladies returning from Lady Wang’s apartments. Baochai was telling them how Xiangling had composed a poem in her dream and talked in her sleep. They were all laughing when they looked up and saw her approaching. At once they clamored to see the poem—but for what followed, read the next chapter.
